he: וְכוּלָּן שֶׁעָשׂוּ מִשֶּׁעָלָה עַמּוּד הַשַּׁחַר כָּשֵׁר. מְנָהָנֵי מִילֵּי? אָמַר רָבָא: דְּאָמַר קְרָא: ״וַיִּקְרָא אֱלֹהִים לָאוֹר יוֹם״, לַמֵּאִיר וּבָא קְרָאוֹ ״יוֹם״.
en: § The mishna concludes: And with regard to all these things, if one did them after daybreak they are valid. The Gemara asks: From where is this matter derived, that from daybreak it is already considered daytime? Rava said: As the verse states: “And God called the light [or] day” (Genesis 1:5), meaning: To that which was becoming lighter and lighter he called day. The Hebrew word or is not to be understood in its usual sense of light, but as a verbal noun: that which is becoming lighter and lighter. It teaches that as soon as light begins to appear in the sky it is called daytime.
